This handsome revival offers stirring performances and gorgeous staging, but it can't entirely overcome the show's dated gender dynamics.

Like Stanley Kowalski with Stella, the sexual chemistry is too strong for Julie to give up, and when Billy’s wildness leads to the inevitable—or the inevitable for a musical—she prefers to live with the ghost of his power than do without it altogether.

It’s a story mired in archaic, cringe-inducing gender dynamics, and despite Rodgers’s score—which at times is so gorgeous it raises goosebumps—the unavoidable truth is that the play built around Hammerstein’s book and lyrics feels ready either for retirement or radical reenvisioning.
Until then, the show is a miraculous fusion of sentiment and craftsmanship, and even the finale can be made to work by a smart director who isn’t afraid of heartfelt emotion.
